filters.title: Experience
filters.question: How much experience do you have with Linux?

options.text: Beginner: I have never used Linux and need a system that is very easy to learn.
Intermediate: I know the basics of Linux and I am eager to learn more.
Pro: I am very comfortable with Linux and know how to do advanced tasks.

filters.title: Hardware
filters.question: How much RAM does your computer have?

options.text: Low: Under 4GB. I have an older computer and need a system that runs lightly.
Standard: Between 4GB and 8GB. I have a normal, everyday computer.
High: Over 8GB. I have a strong computer with plenty of power.

booleans.title: Nvidia
booleans.question: Do you need the system to handle Nvidia graphics drivers automatically?

options.text: No: I do not use Nvidia, or I prefer to install the drivers myself.
Yes: I have an Nvidia graphics card and need the drivers ready from the start.

booleans.title: Wayland
booleans.question: Do you need modern display features like HDR or advanced scaling?

options.text: No: I have a very simple screen setup and don't need fancy features.
Yes: I want modern visual features like HDR or different refresh rates for my monitors.

matches.title: Preinstalled Software
matches.question: How much software should be installed from the start?

options.text: Minimal: I want an minimal base system so I can install only what I need.
Balanced: I want the standard everyday apps installed for me.
Everything: I want all apps, drivers, and video players ready to go immediately.

matches.title: Full Control
matches.question: Do you prefer having full control or a system that cannot break?

options.text: Full Control: I want to change anything I want, even if I have to fix it myself.
Balanced: I want a normal system that is stable but still lets me change things.
Unbreakable: I want a locked system that prevents me from accidentally breaking it.

matches.title: Update Frequency
matches.question: How often do you want your system to update?

options.text: Rare: I want thoroughly tested updates to ensure my computer never breaks.
Regular: A standard update schedule is perfectly fine for me.
Constant: I want to receive the absolute newest features as soon as possible.

matches.title: Ecosystem
matches.question: What kind of community do you want behind your system?

options.text: Specialized: I am fine with a smaller, newer project that does one thing very well.
Established: I want a popular system with good support and a proven history.
Massive: I want a huge, historic project with endless guides and documentation.

matches.title: Customization
matches.question: How much do you want to change how your system looks?

options.text: None: I want a system that looks great immediately without any extra work.
Basic: I only want to make a few small visual changes here and there.
Extensive: I want to deeply change every single detail of how it looks and works.

matches.title: Input Focus
matches.question: How do you prefer to control your computer?

options.text: Mouse: I prefer to click around and use my mouse for almost everything.
Mixed: I use a normal mix of mouse clicks and basic keyboard shortcuts.
Keyboard: I want to control everything quickly using advanced keyboard shortcuts.

matches.title: Gaming
matches.question: How important is gaming on this system?

options.text: No: I have absolutely no interest in playing games on this computer.
Light: I only play simple games that do not need a lot of power.
Heavy: I want a system that is fully set up to play the newest, biggest games.
